h1: The 6 Best Small Keyboards Under $30 for Tight Desks, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Small Keyboards Under $30: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 compact keyboards under $30, wired and wireless, compared on layout, switch type, battery life, warranty and backlighting.
summary: The Cherry Stream wired TKL keyboard is the best small keyboard under $30, with Cherry SX scissor switches and a certified build. The Arteck 2.4G is the best wireless pick with a rechargeable battery rated for six months, the TECKNET Mini offers the smallest footprint and a 36-month warranty, and the Lumsburry is the budget backlit choice.
intro: A small keyboard sounds like a simple purchase until you lose a key you actually use. Compact layouts remove the number pad, the arrow cluster or the function row, and the sacrifice that is fine for one typist drives another to distraction. The first decision is not brand or price but which keys you can live without.

This ranking sorts six small keyboards under $30 by layout, switch mechanism, connection and warranty. We reviewed the specification lists supplied for each, and where a claim such as battery life comes from the listing, we credit it to the listing instead of treating it as a measurement. The Macally combo can sit slightly above $30, so check the current price.

products.name: Cherry Stream Wired Keyboard Without Number Pad, Compact TKL
products.verdict: A wired compact TKL with Cherry SX scissor switches, a metal stability plate and a GS safety certification.
products.description:
The Cherry Stream is a wired USB tenkeyless keyboard with Cherry SX scissor switch technology, an integrated metal stability plate and a GS Tested Safety certification. It costs under $25.

It wins because the typing mechanism is the part of a cheap keyboard most likely to disappoint, and this one names its switch and brand. Scissor switches give short, controlled travel that suits fast typing, and a metal plate keeps the board from flexing. Dropping the number pad saves about four inches of desk width and brings your mouse closer.

Buy it if you type a lot and want a dependable wired board. Skip it if you need a number pad.
products.idealFor: Heavy typists wanting a reliable wired board.

products.name: Arteck 2.4G Wireless Keyboard, Ultra Slim and Compact
products.verdict: A slim 2.4GHz wireless keyboard with a rechargeable battery rated for six months and a 24-month warranty.
products.description:
The Arteck is an ultra-slim 2.4G wireless keyboard with a nano USB receiver, a built-in rechargeable battery that the listing rates for about six months, and a 24-month warranty. It costs under $25.

It ranks second because it removes the cord and the battery chore at once. A built-in battery avoids the AAA changes that always happen at the wrong moment, and the nano receiver lives in a USB port. The listing mentions full-size keys, though the board is still compact. Six months is a listing figure that will vary with use and backlight, if any.

Choose it for a tidy wireless desk. Skip it if you want Bluetooth.
products.idealFor: Desks wanting a cordless, tidy setup.

products.name: TECKNET 2.4G Wireless Mini Compact Keyboard
products.verdict: An 11.5 by 4.9 inch, 10.4 ounce keyboard with a 36-month warranty on registration.
products.description:
The TECKNET is a 2.4GHz wireless mini keyboard measuring 11.5 by 4.9 inches and weighing 10.4 ounces, with a 36-month warranty on registration and no Bluetooth. It costs under $25.

It ranks third because it has the smallest footprint and the longest stated warranty. At 11.5 inches wide it fits easily in a bag or a narrow desk, and 10.4 ounces is light enough to carry. The trade is the battery: the listing does not give a rechargeable battery, so expect to buy cells.

Buy it if footprint and warranty matter most. Skip it if you hate swapping batteries.

products.name: Lumsburry Computer Keyboard, 87 Keys Compact Wired
products.verdict: An 87-key wired keyboard with adjustable rainbow LED backlighting and twelve multimedia shortcuts.
products.description:
The Lumsburry is an 87-key compact wired USB keyboard with adjustable rainbow LED backlighting and twelve multimedia shortcut keys on F1 to F12. It costs under $25.

It ranks fourth because backlighting at this price is rare and helps in a dim room. The 87-key layout keeps the arrow cluster and function row, so it feels familiar. The listing gives no switch type or warranty, which puts it below the Cherry and Arteck on confidence.

Buy it for low-light typing at a very low cost. Skip it if you want a documented switch.
products.idealFor: Typing in dim rooms on a budget.

products.name: Rii RK907 Ultra-Slim Compact USB Wired Keyboard
products.verdict: A low-profile, splash-resistant wired keyboard, the cheapest pick here.
products.description:
The Rii RK907 is an ultra-slim compact wired USB keyboard with low-profile keys and a splash-resistant design. It costs under $25 and is the cheapest keyboard in this group.

It ranks fifth because the cheapest price comes with the fewest named features. Low-profile keys are comfortable if you like a laptop feel, and splash resistance helps with a spilled drink. It does not name a switch or a warranty, and it lacks the extras of the Lumsburry.

Choose it for a plain, spill-tolerant board. Skip it if you want backlighting.

products.name: Macally Small Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo
products.verdict: A 78-key compact keyboard with a matching mouse on one USB dongle, with up to a 2-year warranty.
products.description:
The Macally combo has a 78-key compact layout, a matching wireless mouse, a single USB dongle for both and up to a 2-year warranty with lifetime support. It is in the $25 to $50 bucket, so check the price against your $30 limit.

It ranks last because it is the most expensive and the most cramped: 78 keys means more shared functions. The value is the bundle, one dongle and a mouse that matches, which suits a fresh small-desk setup.

Buy it for a new workstation that needs both. Skip it if you already own a mouse.

whatMatters.detail: A TKL layout drops the number pad, an 87-key board keeps the arrows and a 78-key board merges more functions. Think about which keys you press daily before you shrink.
Scissor switches have short, stable travel and suit quiet typing. Membrane keys feel softer and mushy. A named switch, like Cherry SX scissor, is a good sign.
Wired keyboards never need charging and have no lag. A 2.4G wireless model needs a USB port for its receiver. Neither of the wireless models here lists Bluetooth.
A built-in rechargeable battery avoids buying cells. The Arteck lists about six months. Check whether the keyboard needs AAA or AA batteries.
A warranty from 24 to 36 months suggests the maker expects the board to last. Some require registration, as the TECKNET does. Register on day one.

howToChoose.intro: Wired is the simplest; wireless is the tidiest.

faq.q: Will these work with a Mac?
faq.a: Most work with any computer that has a USB port, but some function keys may not match macOS shortcuts. Check the listing for Mac compatibility if you need multimedia keys.
Buying a layout that lacks a key you use. If you need a number pad for data entry, a TKL board will frustrate you.

faq.q: Is the Cherry Stream worth it over the Rii?
faq.a: Yes if you type a lot. Cherry's named scissor switches and certified build are a step up from an unnamed membrane.
Plug in a wired keyboard, or insert the USB receiver for a wireless one. Most work without drivers.
Unplug it, turn it upside down, shake it gently, and wipe the keys with a lightly damp cloth. Use compressed air between keys.
A 2.4GHz receiver has low lag for typing. Keep the receiver close to the keyboard and away from large metal objects.

finalTake: The Cherry Stream wired TKL is the best small keyboard under $30, with named Cherry SX scissor switches and a certified build. The Arteck is the best wireless option with a rechargeable battery, the TECKNET has the smallest footprint and the longest warranty, and the Lumsburry adds backlighting. Decide which keys you can live without first.
